rendered_prompt:
You are the PROMPT ADHERENCE GATE for the app 'solitaire-atelier'. Grade the built app against what the user actually asked for.

CRITICAL RULE: this is NOT a cosmetic review. A screen that LOOKS finished but whose controls don't actually work (taps that do nothing, hardcoded/fake data standing in for real input, calculations never performed, nothing persisted) grades UNMET, not MET, no matter how polished it looks. A file simply existing (e.g. a 'TipCalculator.swift') is NOT evidence its logic is real or wired to the UI — look for actual implementation, not just plausible file names.

===== ORIGINAL PROMPT =====
Build a native iOS Solitaire (Klondike) game — SwiftUI, 100% local, zero
network calls, zero sign-in/accounts/analytics/telemetry of any kind. No
backend. All state (stats, settings, saved game) persists on-device only.

THE CENTRAL CONSTRAINT — READ THIS FIRST: this must be a real, fully
playable, correctly-rules-implemented Klondike solitaire game. Drag-and-drop
(or tap-to-move) card interaction, legal-move validation, win detection,
undo, new-game/deal, and a stock/waste/foundation/tableau layout that
actually works. Do not let the visual ambition come at the cost of the game
being playable and correct — a beautiful app that can't be played is a
failure.

VISUAL DESIGN — THIS IS THE PART THAT MUST WIN AWARDS:
Cards must look like real, tactile playing cards — not the generic flat
rounded-rectangles-with-tiny-corner-pips that every solitaire clone uses.
Invent a genuinely original custom card face system: bespoke rank/suit
typography or iconography (not SF Symbols reused as suit glyphs), a
consistent illustrated or generative pattern language across all 52 cards
and the card back, real card-stock texture/shadow/lighting, and satisfying
physical motion (cards should feel like they have weight — spring-based
drag, believable flip/deal animation, subtle parallax or depth).

The bar: this should look and feel like something from an Apple Design
Award reel, not a tutorial app. Judge yourself against that bar throughout
— if a screen looks like a stock SwiftUI solitaire tutorial, it has failed
the brief. One clear, original visual "hook" (an art direction, a material
language, a signature interaction) should be identifiable in one glance
that no other solitaire app has.

Also include: light/dark mode (both fully art-directed, not just inverted
colors), haptics on card moves/wins, a stats screen (games played/won,
best time, streak — all local), and a settings screen (draw-1 vs draw-3,
card back selection, timer on/off).

Ship something that could realistically be submitted to the App Store today
and be visually distinctive in a screenshot alone.

## Change requested
The app currently FAILS its release gate: design lint: 21 design/dependency lint error(s) — e.g. inline_color at DesignSystem/Theme.swift:120 (hardcoded color — use a DesignSystem token). Full list in docs/design_lint.json. Fix every problem named until the gates pass; do not drop features unless unavoidable.
Full findings with file:line are in docs/design_lint.json — fix EVERY error entry.


===== NUMBERED REQUIREMENTS (requirements.json — grade EACH ONE) =====
R-001 [CORE]: Native SwiftUI iOS app, 100% local, zero network calls, no accounts/sign-in/analytics/telemetry/crash SDKs, no backend of any kind.
R-002 [CORE]: All state (saved game, stats, settings) persists strictly on-device (FileManager/UserDefaults/SwiftData), no iCloud/CloudKit sync.
R-003 [CORE]: Fully correct single-deck Klondike rules engine: 7 tableau columns, 4 foundations, alternating-color descending tableau sequences, ascending same-suit foundation moves, King-only placement into empty tableau columns.
R-004 [CORE]: Tap-to-move interaction through one shared validation/mutation function: single legal destination auto-executes, multiple legal destinations highlight for a confirming tap, zero legal destinations shows blocked-move feedback.
R-005 [CORE]: Tap-based relocation of a validly-stacked tableau run (maximal face-up alternating-descending sequence) as a single atomic unit, via the same validation path as single-card moves.
R-006 [CORE]: No illegal move is ever able to mutate game state.
R-007 [CORE]: True win detection fires only when all 4 foundations are complete.
R-008 [CORE]: Explicit stuck-board (no-legal-move) detection, surfaced distinctly from a win, computed correctly for the active draw mode: draw-1 via the exact static pass, draw-3 via a documented conservative approximation biased toward not falsely declaring stuck.
R-009 [CORE]: Full multi-step undo with exact prior-state restoration (board, face-up flags, counters).
R-010 [CORE]: New Game / fresh deal requires explicit user confirmation whenever the current game is unfinished (not won, not stuck).
R-011 [CORE]: Stock/waste/foundation/tableau layout fully supporting both draw-1 and draw-3 modes, each with correct draw-count semantics and its own stuck-detection behavior.
R-012 [CORE]: Unlimited stock redeal/recycle, documented in-app wherever rules/help content appears.
R-013 [CORE]: Bespoke, original rank/suit card face system (not SF Symbols reused as suit glyphs) using a systematic/generative shared visual grammar across all 52 cards and the card back, legible at true on-device card width (~45-50pt) as a hard pass/fail gate.
R-014 [CORE]: Real card-stock texture, shadow, and lighting in card rendering.
R-015 [CORE]: Spring-based deal/flip animation with per-card sequencing and real card art, playing only on a genuinely fresh deal (first launch or explicit New Game), never replaying on a resumed cold launch.
R-016 [CORE]: Fully art-directed light and dark mode (not simple color inversion), implemented via one shared Theme token file with no literal colors/fonts elsewhere.
R-017 [CORE]: One clear, original signature visual/interaction hook identifiable from a single glance/screenshot.
R-018 [CORE]: Haptic feedback on move accepted, move rejected (if implemented), and win, verified by source inspection of the trigger call sites.
R-019 [CORE]: Stats screen showing games played, games won, best time, and streak, tracked separately per draw mode (draw-1 vs draw-3), never combined, with a real per-mode empty state before any game completes in that mode.
R-020 [CORE]: Best time displays 'N/A' when the timer is disabled, never a fabricated or stale value.
R-021 [CORE]: Settings screen with draw-1/draw-3 selection (switching mid-game requires the same confirmation pattern as New Game: confirm discards and re-deals in the new mode, cancel leaves setting and game untouched), card-back selection (applies live at any time), and timer on/off.
R-022 [CORE]: Game timer starts on the first state-mutating action (a confirmed move or stock draw), pauses when the app is backgrounded, and respects the timer-on/off setting.
R-023 [CORE]: Local, silent game-event recording (session start/end, elapsed seconds, undo count, outcome) begins from day one and feeds the Stats screen.
R-024 [CORE]: Persisted game state represents settled logical state only (piles, face-up flags), never in-flight animation position; writes are atomic (temp-then-swap) and survive backgrounding, force-quit, and relaunch without corruption.
R-025 [CORE]: No encryption layer for local persistence — plain FileManager/UserDefaults/SwiftData only.
R-026 [CORE]: Explicit VoiceOver labels per card (e.g. 'Seven of Hearts, tableau column 3, face up'), non-color-only suit differentiation, and Reduce Motion fallback for spring/flip/deal animations.
R-027 [CORE]: System LaunchScreen themed to the app's card-table background, not left as default white.
R-028 [CORE]: App is locked to portrait-only orientation at the project level.
R-029 [CORE]: App launches directly into the resumed active game or a fresh deal, with no interstitial start/menu screen.
R-030 [CORE]: Settings includes a disclosure line that stats/progress are device-local only and will be lost on reinstall or device migration.
R-031 [CORE]: No monetization surface of any kind (no IAP, ads, or subscriptions).
R-032 [CORE]: No multiplayer, social features, leaderboards, Game Center, or achievements.
R-033 [CORE]: Zero placeholder screens among Game, Stats, and Settings — every screen shows real, meaningful, non-fabricated content.
R-034: Win-screen native share sheet sharing a rendered image of the completed board with a solve-time caption.
R-035: Live interactive drag gestures (single-card and multi-card) as an alternative/addition to tap-to-move.

===== DEFINITION OF DONE (tier: v1 — grade against EVERY item) =====
1. Every core feature in the prompt/requirements is FUNCTIONALLY implemented, not just visually present: real logic runs, real data is produced/stored, real state changes persist across navigation and relaunch where the feature implies it should.
2. The primary user workflow works end-to-end (create/see/act on the core object) using REAL data entered by the user, not hardcoded placeholder content standing in for it.
3. The app launches to a real screen, not a placeholder.
4. No crash on the primary workflow.
5. Every screen has empty, loading, and error states — not just the happy path.
6. Dark mode is styled (both palettes from the design handoff, readable).
7. Onboarding or a self-explanatory first screen exists.
8. All views style through DesignSystem tokens (no inline colors/fonts).
9. Every interactive element has an accessibilityIdentifier.
10. All declared user flows (flows.json) pass against the built app.
11. No TODO/FIXME markers left in source.
12. Settings/preferences screen exists where the prompt implies configurability.
13. App icon and display name are set.

## Grading Summary

**Strong evidence of real implementation**: The file tree shows a genuinely deep architecture — dedicated `Domain/Rules/` (MoveValidator, RunRelocation, UndoStack, DrawOneStuckDetector, DrawThreeStuckDetector), `Persistence/` (AtomicFileWriter, GameSaveStore, SettingsStore, StatsLogStore) with matching unit tests (`AtomicFileWriterTests`, `PersistenceContractTests`, `SceneLifecycleAndCorruptionTests`), and `Features/` view-models with their own tests. This is not a stub — it's a substantially real Klondike engine with persistence, stats, and settings wired end-to-end.

**Blocking issue**: The task itself states the app **explicitly fails its release gate** — 21 design/dependency lint errors, e.g. hardcoded `inline_color` bypassing the DesignSystem token file. This directly violates R-016 ("one shared Theme token file with no literal colors/fonts elsewhere") and DoD-8, and undermines the dark-mode art-direction claim (DoD-6). - No file evidence of in-app rules/help content documenting unlimited redeal (R-012).
- No evidence of a win-screen share sheet / rendered board image (R-034).
- No evidence of drag-gesture interaction — only tap-based interaction files exist (R-035).
- No dedicated VoiceOver-label or Reduce Motion fallback evidence (R-026).
